title: Navigating the unpredictability of everything: strategy when you can't predict the future
summary: Jason Cohen shows that even elite experts fail at forecasting markets, sales, winners and products, then lays out how to build strategy anyway. Have a strategy, follow customer behavior (especially product "abuse"), and use moats, optionality, hedges and bets on what won't change.

principles.text: A strategy is required even when it's wrong; it gives direction and produces something interesting that early fans can reveal the real answer through.
principles.quote: A strategy gives you a direction. A direction creates something interesting. Something interesting might be used by zealous early fans, even if it ends up uncovering the answer rather than being the answer.

principles.text: Decide and move forward rather than deliberating, because deliberation assumes we can reason about the future, and gain experience instead.
principles.quote: Making a decision and moving forward is often more effective than extended deliberation about the decision.

principles.text: Follow customer behavior to upgrade your strategy; treat requests as signals of intent, not as the new strategy itself.
principles.quote: Customers are where you discover how to upgrade your strategy. Since you know your initial strategy is wrong, following customers' lead is how you correct it.

principles.text: When customers abuse your product to do something else, that's a strong signal to change strategy. Code Historian's peer-review abuse became Code Collaborator, 97% of company revenue.
principles.quote: "Abuse" is a strong, positive signal for customer demand, and worthy of a change in strategy.

principles.text: Build a plan out of "or" not "and": create optionality with many ways to succeed, since a plan needing everything to go right rarely works.
principles.quote: A resilient plan is built of "or" not "and."

principles.text: Bet on what will not change (e.g. fast, cheap, secure) rather than predicting what will, and leverage your own existing strengths.
principles.quote: it is difficult to predict how the future will change, but it can be easy to predict the ways the future will *not* change.
